paper.title_en: Strong decays of $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$ and $ψ(4160)$ in four relativistic wave-function representations
paper.abstract_en: Strong decays provide a direct test of the relativistic structure of heavy quarkonium wave functions. We study the OZI-allowed hadronic decays of the vector charmonia $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$ and $ψ(4160)$ within the Salpeter equation, using four relativistic wave-function representations $φ_1$--$φ_4$ that differ in the $S$-, $P$- and $D$-wave components they retain independently, and the revised ${}^3P_0$ model. The quark-pair creation strength is fixed once, by reproducing the measured $ψ(3770)\to D\bar D$ width, and is not readjusted afterwards, so that the results for the two higher states are parameter-free predictions. The representation $φ_2$ predicts $94^{+34}_{-23}$~MeV for $ψ(4040)$ and $100^{+23}_{-20}$~MeV for $ψ(4160)$, in agreement with the measured $84.5\pm12.3$ and $69\pm10$~MeV, and it is the only one whose predicted width ratios are compatible with the data. By contrast, $φ_1$ overshoots $ψ(4040)$ by $2.5σ$, $φ_3$ gives the largest widths and is disfavoured at the $5σ$ level, and $φ_4$, which has no independent $S$-wave component, underestimates $ψ(3770)$ by about $2σ$ and cannot be applied to final states containing vector mesons. These results show that a successful representation must contain independent $S$, $P$ and $D$ components, the $P$-wave terms providing the dominant relativistic correction, while the nodal structure of the wave functions accounts for the large uncertainties of the predictions. The mixing angles extracted from $φ_2$, $7.92^{\circ}$, $25.8^{\circ}$ and $26.3^{\circ}$, agree with the values obtained in coupled-channel models.
